amazon.profile: Amazon Web Services is the cloud computing business of Amazon.com, Inc., based in Seattle. It develops campuses of its own and also takes large wholesale leases from third-party developers. Company figures give 39 Regions and 123 Availability Zones, a zone sometimes covering several separate buildings rather than one, plus more than 750 CloudFront points of presence and 15 regional edge caches.
amazon.publishedFacilities: 39 Regions and 123 Availability Zones (plus announced plans for 2 more Regions in Saudi Arabia and Chile, and 7 more AZs), stated on aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/, fetched 2026-08-02. AWS does not publish a count of individual buildings.

apple.profile: Apple Inc. is an American consumer electronics and services company listed on Nasdaq. Its data centres are enterprise infrastructure, not colocation: they carry iCloud, the App Store, Maps, Siri and Apple Music, and no space is sold to third parties. Owned sites are known in North Carolina, Oregon, Nevada, Arizona, Iowa and Denmark. Apple publishes no facility list and supplements owned capacity with leased colocation.

centersquare.profile: Csquare is a North American colocation operator controlled by Brookfield Infrastructure. It was assembled in 2024 when Brookfield's Evoque business took over Cyxtera through that company's Chapter 11 process; the combination traded as Centersquare before shortening its name to Csquare in 2025. Its own site counts 80 data centres, 3.5 million square feet and over 500 MW across 16 North American markets plus London.
centersquare.publishedFacilities: "80 advanced colocation data centers", plus 500+ MW, 3.5M sq ft and 2,000+ customers, all stated on the csquare.com homepage

cogent.profile: Cogent Communications is an internet backbone and IP transit provider headquartered in Washington, DC, and listed on NASDAQ as CCOI. Its facility estate grew sharply after the 2023 purchase of Sprint's wireline business from T-Mobile. Cogent owns and operates the sites itself, selling rack space alongside transit, and publishes a count of 87 internet data centres across North America and Europe.
cogent.publishedFacilities: "87 Internet data centers" stated on https://www.cogentco.com/en/about-cogent; the company's own location index gives 87 owned and operated across North America (68) and Europe (19), plus 86 Edge Data Centers in North America

cologix.profile: Cologix runs carrier-neutral colocation and interconnection sites in the United States and Canada, plus a larger-format line it markets as Scalelogix. The infrastructure investor Stonepeak has held a majority stake since 2017. The company is headquartered in Denver and reports about 2,000 customers served from more than 45 facilities in 13 markets across the two countries.
cologix.publishedFacilities: "45+ data centers" and "seven hyperscale capacity facilities", stated on https://cologix.com/about-us/

coreweave.profile: Cloud provider specialising in GPU compute for AI and other accelerated workloads, founded in 2017 and based in Livingston, New Jersey. It listed on Nasdaq as CRWV in March 2025 and has no corporate parent. Capacity comes from a mix of leased third-party halls and self-developed sites; the company cites 49 data centres in North America and Europe, over 1 GW active.
coreweave.publishedFacilities: 49 — coreweave.com/ai-data-centers states "49 state-of-the-art AI data centers" across North America and Europe, with 1 GW+ active power and 3.5 GW+ contracted. The page gives no per-site list.

cyrusone.parent: KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners (joint owners)
cyrusone.profile: CyrusOne is a data centre developer and operator based in Dallas, Texas. It listed on Nasdaq as a real estate investment trust before KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners took it private in March 2022 for about $15 billion. It leases mainly large wholesale halls to cloud and enterprise tenants, and reports over 60 operating facilities across nine countries.
cyrusone.publishedFacilities: "60+ operational data centers" on the cyrusone.com homepage; the /data-centers index itself links to 46 individual facility pages

databank.profile: DataBank is a Dallas-based colocation and interconnection operator serving enterprise and mid-market customers across United States metros, with one European presence in the United Kingdom. Its locations page counts 76 data centres, roughly 5 million square feet and about 1 GW of critical IT load. DigitalBridge assembled the company in 2016; AustralianSuper led a $2 billion equity raise in 2024.
databank.publishedFacilities: 76 — the counter block on https://www.databank.com/data-centers/ reads "76 Total Data Centers", alongside 4.98M IT square footage and 1GW critical IT load. The older About page (https://www.databank.com/about-databank/) still says "65+ data centers" and "20 major interconnect hubs".

digital realty.profile: Digital Realty Trust is a real estate investment trust listed on the New York Stock Exchange as DLR, headquartered in Austin, Texas, after relocating from San Francisco. It builds and leases data centre capacity at both wholesale and retail scale, and absorbed the European operator Interxion in 2020. Its locations page counts more than 300 facilities across over 55 metros.
digital realty.publishedFacilities: "300+ Data Centers" and "55+ Global Metros" on https://www.digitalrealty.com/data-centers

edgeconnex.profile: EdgeConneX, founded in 2009, develops wholesale and build-to-suit data centres from a head office in Herndon, Virginia, with regional bases in Amsterdam and Singapore. EQT Infrastructure acquired the company in 2020 and still owns it. By its own count it has upward of 90 sites completed or under development, spanning 40 kW to more than 500 MW, and it holds an Indian joint venture, AdaniConneX.
edgeconnex.publishedFacilities: "over 90 data centers sustainably built and in development" on https://www.edgeconnex.com/company/about-edgeconnex/; the global map page states "80+ Data Centers", "60+ Unique Markets", "4 Continents", "20+ Countries"; deployments described as 40 kW to 500 MW or more

equinix.profile: Equinix is a data centre operator headquartered in Redwood City, California, and traded on Nasdaq under EQIX. It converted to a real estate investment trust in 2015. Its business is carrier-neutral colocation and interconnection: tenants rent cabinet space and buy cross-connects to networks and cloud providers. The company's site reports 281 facilities across 77 markets.
equinix.publishedFacilities: "280+ Data centers / Across 77 markets on every continent" on the equinix.com homepage; "281 Data Centers" on https://www.equinix.com/about

exa infrastructure.profile: EXA Infrastructure is a London-based wholesale fibre and colocation operator owned by the investment firm I Squared Capital, which created it in September 2021 by buying GTT Communications' infrastructure division. Its estate is network-led rather than retail: the company publishes 174,500 km of fibre reaching 37 countries, more than 500 optical points of presence, and over 270 edge and network colocation sites.
exa infrastructure.publishedFacilities: "270+ Edge and network colocation sites" and "500+" optical points of presence, stated on https://exainfra.net/our-network/, alongside 174,500 km of fibre, 300+ cities connected and 6,000+ metro route km; the colocation page states 22 submarine cable landing stations built and operated

flexential.profile: Flexential is a United States colocation, interconnection and cloud provider based in Charlotte, North Carolina, formed in 2017 when GI Partners combined its Peak 10 and ViaWest holdings; the current name dates from 2018. GI Partners still controls it, with Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners investing in 2024. Its site lists more than 40 data centres across 18 US markets.
flexential.publishedFacilities: 40+ — the stat row on https://www.flexential.com/data-centers reads "40+ data centers / 18 US markets / 3M+ sq. ft. footprint / 100+ Gbps network backbone". The same page lists individual facilities with square footage and MW (e.g. Atlanta - Douglasville 2, 358,000 sq ft, 36 MW).

gds.profile: GDS Holdings Limited is a Chinese developer and operator of colocation data centres, listed on Nasdaq under GDS and in Hong Kong as 9698. It builds carrier-neutral facilities in and around Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hong Kong, serving cloud providers and large internet companies. It reported 668,283 square metres of area in service at the end of 2025, and retains a minority stake in DayOne, its former international arm.
gds.publishedFacilities: Not published on gds-services.com. GDS FY2025 results reporting cites 504,843 sqm of data centre area in service at end-2025 and 670,105 sqm committed/pre-committed — seen only in search-result summaries of the FY2025 results, not fetched directly (investors.gds-services.com timed out on fetch).

global switch.profile: Carrier- and cloud-neutral colocation operator running one campus in each of seven cities: Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, London, Madrid, Paris and Singapore, with Johor and Bangkok announced. Its sites sit inside metropolitan connectivity hubs rather than on out-of-town land; the London campus is in Docklands. The company cites over three decades of operation and does not publish its ownership.
global switch.publishedFacilities: Seven operating cities and two announced - listed at globalswitch.com/data-centres/ (Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, London, Madrid, Paris, Singapore; Johor and Bangkok Coming Soon).

google.profile: Google LLC, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. and headquartered in Mountain View, California, designs and operates its own data centre campuses for search, advertising, YouTube and Google Cloud. Its public locations page counts 30 active sites across 11 countries, with further campuses under construction. Google supplements owned capacity with leased space and separately publishes a larger list of cloud regions.
google.publishedFacilities: "30 active locations worldwide" stated on datacenters.google/locations/, fetched 2026-08-02.

iron mountain.profile: Iron Mountain Data Centers is the colocation business of Iron Mountain Incorporated, the New York-listed storage and records-management REIT, and runs as a segment of the parent rather than as a separate company. Its locations page advertises more than 30 sites across three continents, over five million gross square feet and a 1.4 GW portfolio, with clusters in the United States, India, Europe and Singapore.
iron mountain.publishedFacilities: "30+ Locations. 3 Continents. 5M+ Gross SF." as the headline on ironmountain.com/data-centers/locations; the same section elsewhere cites a 1.4 GW portfolio. The locations page renders 24 distinct facility links

lumen.profile: Lumen Technologies is a US telecommunications carrier listed on the NYSE as LUMN and headquartered in Denver, Colorado; it took the Lumen name in 2020, having traded as CenturyLink. It sold its enterprise colocation business in 2017 and now markets network colocation attached to its fibre routes, citing more than 200 North American locations across over 120 cities.
lumen.publishedFacilities: "200+ locations in North America" and "120+ cities offering colocation", stated on https://www.lumen.com/en-us/services/colocation.html

meta.profile: Meta Platforms, Inc., headquartered in Menlo Park, California, builds data centres for its own workloads — Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and AI training — rather than selling cloud capacity to outside customers. Its public locations index names 31 campuses: 26 in the United States, three in Europe, one in Canada and one in Singapore. Announced work includes a Louisiana site being expanded toward five gigawatts.
meta.publishedFacilities: 31 locations enumerated at datacenters.atmeta.com/all-locations/, fetched 2026-08-02. Meta states no total on the page; 31 is the count of named entries.

microsoft.profile: Microsoft Corporation, of Redmond, Washington, runs data centres mainly for Azure and for its own software services. It builds its own capacity and also signs large wholesale leases with third-party developers. Microsoft's Azure infrastructure page claims more than 80 regions and over 500 data centres, more than 275,000 miles of fibre and subsea cable, and upwards of 190 network points of presence.
microsoft.publishedFacilities: "80+ Azure regions | 500+ datacenters" stated on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/explore/global-infrastructure, fetched 2026-08-02.

nlighten.profile: European edge colocation operator assembled from regional data centre businesses, registered as nLighten HQ BV in Schiphol-Rijk, the Netherlands. It runs small facilities close to users rather than a few large campuses, across Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, and sells colocation, connectivity and on-site services. It does not publish its ownership.
nlighten.publishedFacilities: 33 edge locations - listed at nlighten.com/en/edge-location/ across Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, Switzerland and the UK.

ntt.profile: NTT Global Data Centers is the data centre arm of NTT DATA, part of Japan's NTT group. It was assembled from acquired regional operators including e-shelter in Germany, Gyron in the UK, and RagingWire in the United States. It sells colocation and wholesale capacity, and reports more than 160 facilities in over 20 countries and above 2,000 MW of IT load.
ntt.publishedFacilities: "we operate over 160 data centers in more than 20 countries and regions" and "2,000MW+ critical IT load in over 20 countries" on https://services.global.ntt/en-us/services-and-products/global-data-centers

oracle.profile: Oracle Corporation, an American enterprise software and database vendor listed on the New York Stock Exchange, runs Oracle Cloud Infrastructure alongside its applications business, building some regions and leasing others. A region holds between one and three availability domains, and a single domain can sit in more than one physically separate building. Oracle's documentation counts 52 commercial OCI regions, with government and dedicated realms listed separately.
oracle.publishedFacilities: Oracle publishes regions, not individual buildings: 52 commercial (OC1 realm) cloud regions are listed in the table at https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/General/Concepts/regions.htm. Oracle states a region contains one to three availability domains and an availability domain is one or more data centres, so the building count is not derivable from the published figures.

qts.profile: QTS is a data centre operator founded in 2003 that develops large campuses in North America and Europe, with hyperscale, enterprise and US federal customers. It traded as the REIT QTS Realty Trust until Blackstone funds bought it for $10 billion in a deal completed in 2021, and it has been privately held since. Its site counts more than 30 facilities and now uses the domain q.com.
qts.publishedFacilities: "Across 30+ facilities", stated in the "By the numbers" block on the q.com homepage; the /data-centers/ finder itself lists more (paginated)

stack.parent: IPI Partners, acquired by Blue Owl Capital
stack.profile: Hyperscale and wholesale data centre developer operating in the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific. It is a portfolio company of IPI Partners, the data centre investment platform Blue Owl Capital agreed to acquire in 2024. In April 2025 Apollo-managed funds bought STACK's seven-site European colocation business, which drops the STACK name. Its locations page cites 8.5 GW built and under development.
stack.publishedFacilities: No facility count published. stackinfra.com/locations/ names 22 markets (10 Americas, 5 Asia Pacific, 7 EMEA) and cites "8.5+ GW Built & Under Development" plus "7.5+ GW Planned & Potential Development".

stt.profile: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres is a Singapore-headquartered carrier-neutral colocation operator, founded in 2014 by ST Telemedia, part of the Temasek group. It reports more than 100 data centres and 2.7 GW of IT load across 12 markets in Asia and Europe, its UK arm trading as VIRTUS Data Centres. In February 2026 KKR and Singtel agreed to buy out ST Telemedia, taking 75% and 25%.
stt.publishedFacilities: 100+ — the "Global reach, local expertise" panel on https://www.sttelemediagdc.com/ publishes "Major business markets 20+ / Data centres worldwide >100 / IT load (GW) 2.7", with a per-country breakdown: India 34, UK 17, Germany 13, Indonesia 9, Philippines 9, Singapore 6, Thailand 3, Malaysia 3, Japan 2, Vietnam 2, South Korea 1, Italy 1.

switch.profile: Colocation operator based in Las Vegas, founded by Rob Roy, known for large campuses it calls PRIMES and for its own Tier 5 facility rating. DigitalBridge and IFM Investors took the company private in December 2022 in a transaction valued near $11 billion, ending its NYSE listing. Its locations page lists five campuses in Nevada, Michigan, Georgia and Texas.
switch.publishedFacilities: 5 campuses ("PRIMES") listed on switch.com/locations/: The Citadel (Tahoe Reno), The Pyramid Campus (Grand Rapids), The Core Campus (Las Vegas), The Keep Campus (Atlanta), The Rock Campus (Austin). The page gives acreage (3,058 US West, 2,418 US East) but no building count or MW figure.

telehouse.profile: Telehouse is the data centre brand of KDDI, the Japanese telecommunications group, and operates carrier-neutral colocation sites rather than cloud services. Its first facility opened in New York in 1989; the London Docklands campus followed in 1990. Several major internet exchanges, including France-IX, HKIX and JPIX, are hosted in its buildings. Telehouse states it runs more than 40 data centres across over 20 cities in more than 10 countries.
telehouse.publishedFacilities: "40+ Data centres in more than 20 cities, in more than 10 countries" — stated on https://www.telehouse.net/about-telehouse/telehouse-data-centre-colocation-services/. The global list at telehouse.com/global-data-centers/ enumerates roughly 23 individual facilities across about 15 cities.

tierpoint.profile: TierPoint is a privately held United States provider of colocation, managed IT and cloud services, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri. It dates from a 2010 Dallas data centre purchase by Cequel III and grew mainly by acquisition. Shareholders include Cequel III, RedBird Capital Partners, Thompson Street Capital Partners, the Stephens Group and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan. The company lists 40 data centres in 20 US markets.
tierpoint.publishedFacilities: 40 — "40 world-class data centers across 20 U.S. markets, coast-to-coast" on https://www.tierpoint.com/about-us/, and "our 40 world-class data centers are connected coast-to-coast" on https://www.tierpoint.com/data-centers/, which also enumerates facilities by state (e.g. five in Pennsylvania, three in Texas, four in North Carolina).

vantage.profile: Wholesale data centre developer and operator founded in 2010 around a Santa Clara campus. DigitalBridge holds control alongside Silver Lake following a $9.2 billion equity round completed in June 2024; AustralianSuper, GIC and ADIA hold further stakes. Builds large campuses leased mainly to hyperscale tenants. Its locations page counts 41 campuses across five continents.
vantage.publishedFacilities: 41 campuses — the header of vantage-dc.com/data-center-locations/ reads "5 continents. 41 campuses." Regional sub-pages name 12 North America, 15 EMEA and 9 APAC campuses.

virtus.profile: Carrier-neutral wholesale and colocation operator, part of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres. Its estate is concentrated on interconnected London campuses - Slough, Stockley Park, Hayes, Enfield and Saunderton - with more recent expansion into Berlin and Milan. Facilities are built to Tier III standard, and the campus model is sold on site diversity within one metro.
virtus.publishedFacilities: 20 location pages - listed at virtusdatacentres.com/locations/, covering London campuses at Slough, Stockley Park, Hayes, Enfield and Saunderton, Berlin at Marienpark and Wustermark, and Milan.
